transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We've got six weeks reserved for the API gateway technical-debt work before the next major product launch, and I have final approval authority on the plan. I've reviewed the current draft — it starts with gateway log cleanup, assigns one backend engineer and two platform engineers, but notably it doesn't contain any dated security or cost-control commitments. Before I can approve this, our quarterly planning routine requires backend engineering, reliability, security, and FinOps to record any material findings in the decision log and give a final review. So I'd like to go around and get input from each of those areas. Let's start with what you're all seeing and any concerns you have with the draft as it stands.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While tracing an unrelated customer timeout this morning, I confirmed that the gateway's retry shortcut can issue repeated upstream calls, and it has pushed the affected endpoint's p99 latency above 900 ms. I hadn't filed the technical-debt item yet because I was still reproducing it, but I'm confident in the finding now and it should be recorded in the decision log before we finalize this plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a staffing concern before we go further. After the draft plan was circulated, I checked the current on-call roster, and during weeks 2 through 4 we only have one platform engineer available for planned debt work without leaving an uncovered overnight rotation. The draft assigns two platform engineers, so as it stands we'd either be leaving nights uncovered or falling short on the staffing the plan assumes. I haven't updated the planning document yet, but this needs to go in the decision log before we finalize.

transcript.text: I have a critical security finding to raise. During a separate dependency review, I found that the gateway's tracing agent is affected by a high-severity vulnerability. I've confirmed that its upgrade must be completed by day 10 with a security review. This finding is confirmed but hasn't yet been entered in the central backlog or the decision log. Given that the current draft plan starts with gateway log cleanup and contains no dated security commitments, this upgrade needs to be prioritized and explicitly scheduled with a day-10 deadline before we finalize this plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a material cost-control finding to record. I matched this month's cloud invoice against gateway traffic and found that verbose request logging is causing an avoidable $18,000 per month in egress charges. I confirmed the amount today but haven't posted the billing note yet. The approved debt plan must switch gateway logging to 10-percent sampling to remove that charge. This needs to go into the decision log before we finalize the plan.
